newsitem.title: GERMANY: Coffee use seen rising 2.5 pct per year to 2000.
newsitem.headline: Coffee use seen rising 2.5 pct per year to 2000.

text.p: Coffee consumption is expected to grow at an annual rate of 2.5 percent in the years to 2000, said Pablo Dubois, chief of secretariat services at the International Coffee Organization (ICO).
Dubois, who delivered his forecast at the F.O. Licht coffee conference, stressed this was a personal rather than an official ICO prediction.

"Consumption may rise from approximatley 96 million bags in 1995 to 107.5 million in the year 2000, with the possibility, if this increase is maintained, of reaching 120-121 million in the year 2005," he said.
"This is really accounted for mainly by performance in the emerging markets where the growth rate per annum is about 3.4 percent compared with only 1.4 percent in established markets."
Russian consumption should grow by 11.8 percent a year, with net imports rising to 2.7 million in 2000 from 1994's 1.7 million, Dubois said.
Consumption in China, about 200,000 bags in 1995, could rise to just under one million bags in 2000.
"And because of the analogies of what has happened in Japan or South Korea it is possible that consumption in China, if everything goes right, may reach up to seven million bags by 2005."
